heroHeadline: Krache Dife Gang Attacks IDP Camp in Delmas 6 — 2 Killed Including a Minor, 24 Houses Burned; Day 16 of MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Closure; US Senate Pushes to Extend Haitian TPS Through 2027
heroSubtitle: On May 25, 2026, members of the Krache Dife de Delmas 6 gang — part of the Viv Ansanm coalition — attacked a displaced persons camp in the Delmas 6 corridor of Port-au-Prince, killing 2 people including a minor and burning 24 houses. The attack exemplifies a documented gang tactic of targeting IDP camps to generate secondary displacement and assert territorial control over humanitarian spaces. Approximately 1.5 million Haitians remain internally displaced nationwide, including roughly 30,000 newly displaced since the May 10 gang violence surge in Cité Soleil and the Cul-de-Sac Plain. MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil — the only emergency health facility for the commune's ~300,000 residents — entered its 16th consecutive day of closure with no announced reopening timeline; the intra-Viv Ansanm clash that triggered the May 10 evacuation (Chen Mechan/Taliban/400 Mawozo vs. Duvivier/Pyè 6) continues to prevent safe access. The GSF's ~800-person advance force (400+ Chadian, 75 Guatemalan, 70 Salvadoran; under Mongolian Maj. Gen. Erdenebat Batsuuri since May 14) remains exclusively concentrated in Port-au-Prince city center, providing no coverage to Delmas, Cité Soleil, or the Artibonite. On the political front, Senate advocates launched a push during the week of May 19 to extend Temporary Protected Status for Haitians through 2027 — a lower-threshold legislative effort running parallel to the US Supreme Court's pending ruling in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot, expected by late June or early July 2026. The Court's conservative 6-3 majority appeared at April 29 oral arguments to signal deference to the Trump administration's position that TPS termination is non-reviewable. Approximately 350,000 Haitian TPS holders and ~87,000 US-born children of TPS holders await the outcome while Haiti's humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate. PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 abandonment of the August 30 election date stands unrevised; no electoral decree has been issued; 23 communes remain inaccessible to electoral authorities.
